name: Xata
tagline: Open-source Postgres platform with storage-level copy-on-write branching, scale-to-zero and anonymized clones.
description: Xata began as a serverless spreadsheet-like database with built-in search, but has since rebuilt itself as a PostgreSQL platform focused on development workflows. Its stack runs vanilla Postgres on Kubernetes (CloudNativePG) with storage-level copy-on-write branching, so a production-sized database can be cloned in seconds, optionally with PII anonymized, for previews, testing or AI agents. In April 2026 the core platform was open-sourced under Apache 2.0; Xata Cloud and bring-your-own-cloud deployments are paid, with the old free SaaS tier retired. It also maintains pgroll for zero-downtime, reversible schema migrations. Consider it when realistic staging data and branch-per-PR workflows matter more than a free tier.

pricing.notes: 14-day trial on Xata Cloud; self-hosted open-source edition is free; BYOC on AWS, Azure, GCP or Hetzner by quote.

scale.notes: Standard single-primary Postgres clusters; branches share storage blocks until modified.

strengths: Copy-on-write branches of large databases in seconds
Built-in PII anonymization for realistic staging copies
Runs unmodified Postgres, so extensions and tools work
Open-source core plus BYOC option for data-residency needs
pgroll enables reversible, zero-downtime schema migrations
weaknesses: No permanent free tier on the managed service
Young platform after a full product pivot; old SDKs are deprecated
No horizontal write scaling or multi-region in the open-source edition
useCases: Branch-per-pull-request preview databases with production-like data
Safe environments for AI coding agents
Testing migrations against anonymized production clones
Postgres in your own cloud account with branching
notIdealFor: Very high write throughput needing sharding
Teams without Kubernetes skills wanting to self-host
